title.narrative: UNICEF Jemen: Barns ökade rättigheter och samhällstjänster
UNICEF Yemen: Children's enhanced rights and access to basic services

description.narrative:
Outcome of the programme
The programme aims to ensure that children, adolescent and women in Yemen are better protected and have increased resilience to vulnerabilities which put them at risk of violence, abuse, neglect and harm through a holisic support to respond to the needs of children experiencing child rights violations and ensuring access to basic services.
Outputs 1. Children at risk or those experiencing child rights violations have better access to quality responsive and protective protection services. 2. Children have better access to quality basic services linked to health, nutrition and education to reduce their vulnerabilities to experiencing child rights violations. The programme is designed to suport multi-sectoral interventions to maximize the impact for children, addressing multiple deprivations and vulnerabilities. The programme builds on two components: Component 1: Response to child rights violations targeting the most vulnerable children through the provision of quality preventive and protection services, systems strengthening and capacity development. Component 2: Preventive intervention to reduce vulnerabilities for children at risk of child right violations through the mainstreaming of and access to basic services.

UNICEF Jemen: Stöd till skydd av barn och tillgång till basala samhällstjänster
Insatsen syftar till identifiering av och stödinsatser för utsatta barn. Insatsen ska bidra till bl.a. minskning av barnäktenskap, rekryteringar och barnarbete. I tillägg ges stöd för återintegrering av barn i säkra skolmiljöer, liksom yrkesutbildningar för ungdomar.
Programmet syftar till att säkerställa att barn, ungdomar och kvinnor i Jemen är bättre skyddade, och har ökad motståndskraft mot våld, utnyttjande, negligering och skada. Ett holistiskt stöd skall svara upp mot utsatta barns behov, liksom säkerställa tillgång till grundläggande samhällstjänster.
1. Utsatta barn, liksom barn som överlevt övergrepp, ska få bättre tillgång till skyddstjänster. 2. Barn ska få bättre tillgång till grundläggande samhällstjänster länkade till hälsa, nutrition, samt utbildning för en minskad utsatthet. Programmet är designat till att ge en multi-sektoriell respons för att maximera stödet till barnen, och minska utsattheten.
Programmet består av två komponenter. Komponent 1: Skyddsinsatser för barn som utsatts för övergrepp genom förebyggande och skyddsverksamhet, inklusive genom systemstärkande och kapacitetshöjning av sociala samhällstjänster. Komponent 2: Förebyggande interventioner som minskar risker för utsatthet genom tillgång till grundläggande samhällstjänster, inklusive utbildning.

sector.narrative: Social services (incl youth development and women+ children)

description.narrative:
In 2024, the Swedish support to UNICEF in Yemen contributed to the following results in the area of child protection and education to vulnerable Yemenis:
-3,403 children in contact with the law (13 per cent girls, 87 per cent boys) accessed free legal aid, diversions, and centre and community based reintegration services. -68,208 children (40 per cent girls, 60 per cent boys) received birth certificates. -224,506 children and caregivers (50 per cent female, 50 per cent male) received mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) -26,503 adolescents (66 per cent girls, 34 per cent boys) were supported through life skills education. -15,294 children (38 per cent girls, 62 per cent boys) were reached through case management services. -1,106,721 people (412,147 boys, 405,940 girls, 147,524 men, and 141,110 women benefited from initiatives on women with GBV and harmful practices prevention and mitigation measures. -The Explosive Ordnance Risk Education programme reached a total of 1,769,780 people (462,567 girls and 489,596 boys 401,851 women and 415,766 men).
Some of the achieved results in the education area in 2024, to which Sweden contributed, were: -33,331 out of school children provided with nonformal education opportunities, with 16,286 successfully mainstreamed into formal education. -587,528 children (279,494 girls) benefitted from school rehabilitation. - 397,719 children (189,806 girls) received essential learning materials. - 5,126 (2,326 male and 2,800) teachers and school based staff benefitted from capacity building and training interventions.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
